title: Multi-Agent Orchestration & Consensus
summary: Decide when more agents are worth their token cost and how their outputs should be combined through self-consistency, bounded debate, and orchestrator-worker joins, then diagnose failures with MAST.
objectives: Explain, using published measurements, why multi-agent systems mostly buy capacity through token spend, and identify task shapes that suit or resist parallel agents.
Apply self-consistency voting to fixed-answer tasks and use the agreement rate as an accept-or-escalate signal rather than as proof of correctness.
Describe how multi-agent debate converges, what controls its length, and why a converged answer can still be confidently wrong.
Design an orchestrator-worker join that does not depend on result order or hidden shared state, and classify a failed run with the MAST failure taxonomy.

sections.title: Extra agents mostly buy capacity, and capacity is billed
paragraphs: Anthropic's BrowseComp analysis reported that token usage, tool calls, and model choice explained 95% of measured performance variance, with token usage alone explaining 80%. These are scoped measurements from that study, not a universal law or a live evaluation in this lesson. Source: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system

The same write-up reported approximately four times the tokens for an agent interaction and approximately fifteen times for its multi-agent system. Independent jurisdiction research is a suitable worked example because each worker can finish without waiting for another. Tightly coupled refactoring is a poor fit because workers need shared intermediate state and must merge edits. Compare against a single-agent or best-of-N baseline before paying for parallel capacity. Source: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system
MAST reports minimal benchmark gains in some comparisons with single-agent or best-of-N systems. Agent count is therefore not a quality guarantee. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.13657
Ten jurisdiction lookups can run independently. Ten agents editing one shared function cannot safely do so without an explicit merge protocol, revision policy, and verification step.
sections.callout: If you cannot name independently completable subtasks, extra agents may add coordination cost without useful capacity.

sections.title: Voting: agreement is a confidence signal, not a verdict
paragraphs: Self-consistency samples diverse reasoning paths and selects the most frequent answer from a fixed answer set. Wang et al. reported a 17.9 percentage-point GSM8K gain under the paper's evaluated models and conditions. This lab does not reproduce that benchmark. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171

Agreement is max_votes divided by samples.length. Here, samples.length is the number of submitted, well-shaped samples, including samples whose answer is invalid or outside the declared answer set. Invalid outputs remain in the denominator and trigger escalation because they provide no accepted vote. A strict majority is greater than one half. Ties, invalid outputs, empty answers, duplicate answer-set entries, and non-finite thresholds must be handled explicitly. The lab uses 0.8 as an illustrative policy, not a universal threshold. The paper discusses beginning with 5 to 10 samples, but deployment settings require local evaluation. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171

Votes yes=4, no=2, unclear=1 produce agreement 4/7, approximately 0.571, so the illustrative 0.8 policy escalates. Five yes votes can produce agreement 1.0 while an external record says no. If one submitted sample is invalid, it still contributes to the denominator, so an apparent accepted-vote majority cannot silently become more confident by discarding that sample.
sections.callout: A unanimous answer can be unanimously wrong. Agreement routes work; an external check tests correctness.

sections.title: Debate: agents that read each other can converge on the wrong answer
paragraphs: Du et al. studied independent answers followed by peer-visible updates over rounds and reported gains in their evaluated settings, including a three-agent, two-round configuration. Debate requires a round cap, per-round timeout, overall timeout, convergence definition, and external verification. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14325

The lab passes previous state and peer state to real asynchronous fixture responders. Convergence requires all position and artifact pairs to match. One trace changes to 42 and passes an external check. Another converges immediately on 41 and fails the same check. A timeout prevents waiting forever, but JavaScript promises cannot be forcibly cancelled by this lab, so no external-cancellation claim is made. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14325
Three agents can agree on the same incorrect artifact. Only an answer key, executable test, authoritative record, or other independent check can expose that error.
sections.callout: Convergence is a stopping condition, not a truth condition.

sections.title: Orchestrator-worker joins: make the merge independent of timing
paragraphs: Parallel branches do not automatically share history or state and may complete in nondeterministic order. A portable join therefore treats each result as an explicit, self-identifying message. The lab uses this general pattern and does not claim ADK compatibility. Source: https://adk.dev/agents/workflow-agents/parallel-agents/

The join validates trusted nonempty tenant and revision values, unique worker IDs, required IDs that are a subset of configured workers, immutable input, admission budget, per-run deadline, envelope identity, revision, tenant, and evidence. It records failures and sorts valid envelopes by worker ID. Completion is set inclusion, never a raw count. Anthropic describes bounded delegation and the cost of slow or duplicated work. Source: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system

Configure required workers alpha, beta, and gamma plus optional worker delta. If beta returns a revision-mismatched envelope while alpha, gamma, and delta return valid envelopes, there are still three valid results. A count-only policy incorrectly reports complete because 3 equals 3. Identity-set inclusion correctly reports incomplete because beta is absent.

Use the existing project42-content checkout from its repository root. If you do not have a checkout, create it once with: git clone https://github.com/project42dev/project42-content.git project42-content, then enter it with: cd project42-content. Both labs use the same repository, and no npm install is necessary.
sections.callout: Count required identities, not successful envelopes.

sections.title: Diagnose failures by category before adding agents
paragraphs: MAST describes 14 failure modes in three categories and reports kappa 0.88 inter-annotator agreement over more than 150 traces. Task verification failures include premature termination, missing or incomplete verification, and incorrect verification. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.13657

The count-only join is incorrect verification because a check ran but counting envelopes did not establish required identity coverage. The repair is a set-inclusion predicate and a changed-input regression. MAST reports scoped improvements from verification and role specifications in its studied systems, not a guarantee for this lab. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.13657
Required alpha, beta, gamma plus valid alpha, gamma, delta is not complete. Adding another result cannot prove beta participated. Replacing delta with epsilon must not change that conclusion.

The learner test intentionally fails before repair with: `FAIL learner repair: required worker beta is absent but broken policy returned complete=true`. Its causal feedback is: `CAUSE: three valid envelopes matched the required count, but delta did not satisfy required identity beta`. Edit only `learner/join-policy.js`, function `hasRequiredWorkers`, and form a set from `validResults.map(r => r.workerId)`. Return true only when every required worker ID is present. After the repair, the learner test should report `PASS learner repair: required identities enforced`. The changed-input test should report `PASS changed input: impostor epsilon cannot replace required beta`. The positive control, where beta is valid and optional delta is invalid, must still complete. The equality regression is part of this same lab and should report `PASS equality regression: position and artifact compared as a pair`. Do not replace the learner repair with an unconditional false result.
sections.callout: Classify the mechanism that failed, then repair that mechanism.

activity.title: Repair and stress-test a consensus join
instructions: Use Node.js 22 and the bash commands in the orchestrator-worker-joins section. No install is required. `npm run demo` should print eleven demonstration lines: four vote lines, two debate lines, and five join lines.

Run `npm run demo` and identify the four vote lines, two debate lines, and five join lines. Explain the majority, tie, invalid-output, unanimous-wrong, debate-revision, wrong-convergence, order-independent join, partial-failure, rejected-identity, budget-failure, and deadline-failure cases.

Run `node learner/learner.test.js` before editing. The configured workers are required alpha, beta, and gamma plus optional delta. Beta returns a revision-mismatched envelope, leaving three valid results from alpha, gamma, and delta. Observe that the deliberately broken count-only policy returns `complete=true`. Expected feedback is `FAIL learner repair: required worker beta is absent but broken policy returned complete=true` followed by `CAUSE: three valid envelopes matched the required count, but delta did not satisfy required identity beta`.

Edit only the `hasRequiredWorkers` function in `learner/join-policy.js`. Build a set from `validResults.map(r => r.workerId)` and return true only when every `requiredWorkerId` is present. Compare your repair with `learner/reference/join-policy.solution.js` only after attempting it. Do not weaken strict runtime validation or change the worker configuration.

Rerun `node learner/learner.test.js`, then run `node learner/changed-input.test.js`. The changed-input test replaces delta with epsilon while beta remains invalid. Both negative cases must reject the same-sized set because beta is absent. Expected results are `PASS learner repair: required identities enforced` and `PASS changed input: impostor epsilon cannot replace required beta`. The learner test also contains a positive control where beta is valid and optional delta is invalid. That case must be complete.

Run `npm test` and record the expected main regression line, `PASS main regressions: 22 assertions`. The count comprises 8 self-consistency assertions, 6 ordinary debate assertions, 1 never-resolving timeout assertion, and 7 join assertions. Async rejection checks use `await assert.rejects` rather than `assert.throws`.

Run `node test/consensus-pair.test.js` in the same lab. The equality repair is included in this lab, not delivered separately. It verifies that debate convergence compares position and artifact as a pair. Expected output is `PASS: distinct structured pairs do not converge; identical pairs converge; NUL data is preserved`. Do not edit `src/core.js` for the learner repair.

Explain the voting denominator with the 4 yes, 2 no, 1 unclear example. Agreement is 4/7, approximately 0.571. Include invalid submitted samples in `samples.length`; do not discard them to inflate agreement. Escalate under the illustrative 0.8 threshold.
Design one decision using a fixed answer set or open-ended protocol, with named independent subtasks, bounded budget, stopping or join rule, escalation path, and an external correctness check.

Label the count-only defect as MAST incorrect verification and explain why more agents or debate rounds cannot repair a predicate that verifies quantity instead of required identity coverage. Explain why replacing optional delta with epsilon preserves the negative result, while making beta valid changes the result.
evidence: The eleven-line demo output, the intentional learner failure, the repaired learner pass, the changed-input pass, the expected 22-assertion main regression line, and the equality-regression pass line.
A diff limited to the `hasRequiredWorkers` function in `learner/join-policy.js` that uses required identity set inclusion.
A causal explanation that beta was configured but its invalid envelope was rejected, while optional delta or epsilon kept the valid-result count equal to the required-result count.
A design record naming answer type, mechanism, budget, termination rule, escalation, external check, and MAST diagnosis.
A short voting calculation showing that all submitted well-shaped samples, including invalid outputs, remain in the agreement denominator.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Where could all samples or agents agree while remaining wrong, and what independent check would reveal it?

questions.prompt: What factor explained most measured performance variance in Anthropic's scoped BrowseComp analysis?
questions.explanation: Token usage alone explained 80% in that study; token usage, tool calls, and model choice explained 95%.

questions.prompt: Which task is the weakest fit for parallel agents?
questions.explanation: Tightly interdependent shared-context work has coordination and merge costs.

questions.prompt: When can direct self-consistency voting be used?
questions.explanation: Direct voting requires comparable final answers.

questions.prompt: What should a 4-2-1 vote do under an illustrative 0.8 threshold?
questions.explanation: Agreement is approximately 0.571 and is not proof of correctness.

questions.prompt: What is possible when a debate converges?
choices: It can converge on an incorrect answer
It cannot converge without a moderator

questions.prompt: What must an asynchronous join assume?
questions.explanation: Branches need explicit state transfer and identity-based merging.

questions.prompt: Which MAST case-study change was associated with a 15.6% ProgramDev success increase?
questions.explanation: The reported result is scoped to the paper's ProgramDev study.
